title: The Lighter Brief
overview: Washington is busy after last week's midterms: President Trump offered UFC boss Dana White the press secretary job, and the House may vote this week on impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Beyond politics, there are dogs sniffing out invasive plants, a UK radio station sticking by a Jamaican school, a warm week ahead in Charlotte before a chill, and a fond farewell to a disco-era voice.

stories.headline: Trump Offers UFC's Dana White the Press Secretary Job
stories.summary: President Trump posted on Saturday that he has offered the White House press secretary role to UFC chief Dana White, a longtime friend. White, speaking at a boxing event in London, said he'd fly to Washington for a Monday meeting but didn't say yes. The offer comes during a broader White House shake-up after the midterms.
key_facts: White plans to meet Trump at the White House on Monday.
Trump suggested White bring UFC figures like Khabib Nurmagomedov and Daniel Cormier as assistants.
Katie Zacharia left the press secretary post after five days; Karoline Leavitt departed in August.
Trump named Stephen Miller to replace Susie Wiles as chief of staff.
disputed: Confirmed: Trump made the offer publicly, and White confirmed the Monday meeting.
Unclear: Whether White is seriously considering the job. Asked about his workload, he said, "Yeah, I got a lot of jobs already."
stories.why: The press secretary is the president's main voice to reporters, so who fills it shapes how the White House communicates.

stories.headline: House May Vote on Impeaching Defense Secretary Hegseth This Week
stories.summary: Republican Rep. Thomas Massie plans to introduce an impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, possibly as early as Monday. Likely incoming Speaker Hakeem Jeffries says he's a "hard yes," and Axios reports GOP leaders expect enough Republican defections for it to pass. Representative-elect Nancy Lacore, a retired admiral whom Hegseth removed in 2025, also weighed in.
key_facts: Massie's resolution has eight articles, including an alleged violation of the 1973 War Powers Resolution over the Iran war.
Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in last week's midterms; the new Congress starts in January.
Lacore flipped South Carolina's 1st District and said she was never given a reason for her removal.
Jeffries said House Democrats are not currently focused on impeaching President Trump.
stories.why: This is an early test of how the newly reshaped Congress will act as a check on the administration.

stories.headline: Meet the Woman Behind the Big Dancehall Shows
stories.summary: The Jamaica Observer profiles Cara Burke, founder of Showtime Services, who helped make Mavado & Friends Live at Toronto's Scotiabank Arena happen. Her company works across Jamaica, the UK, the US and Canada. She's now launching a new production and touring division and encouraging women to learn the whole business.
key_facts: The Mavado concert took place on November 5, 2026, with Masicka and Armanii.
The new division is launching with Tenesha Vernon and Shayna Vernon.
stories.why: It's a nice spotlight on the behind-the-scenes people who bring Caribbean music to the world.

stories.headline: UK Radio Station Adopts Hurricane-Hit Jamaican School
stories.summary: Silk Radio UK gave all proceeds from its January radiothon to Dumfries Primary School in St James, which was damaged by Hurricane Melissa. Beyond the roof repairs, the station saw that families needed help with books and uniforms. It has promised a second radiothon in early 2027.
key_facts: The radiothon took place on January 8, 2026.
Reggae artiste Vernal Sage arranged the handover of gifts and uniforms.
Organizers say the school will stay their charity of choice until it's on stable footing.
stories.why: It's a lovely example of a community sticking around for the long haul after the storm.

stories.headline: Remembering First Choice Singer Rochelle Fleming
stories.summary: Rochelle Fleming, founder and lead singer of the 1970s R&B group First Choice, died on November 5 in Philadelphia at age 72, her manager announced. The group's hits included "Armed and Extremely Dangerous," "Dr Love" and "Let No Man Put Asunder," which Mary J. Blige later covered.
key_facts: The group started in high school as the Debonettes.
"Armed and Extremely Dangerous" reached #28 on the Hot 100 in 1973.
Services will be announced later.
stories.why: Her music remains a dance-floor classic, and it might be worth a listen today.

stories.headline: Charlotte: Sunny 70s All Week, Then a Big Chill
stories.summary: Charlotte can expect sunshine and highs around 70 from Sunday through Wednesday, with possible frost along I-40 at night. A cold front Thursday brings a 30% chance of showers, then highs drop to around 60 and lows near 30 by Saturday night.
key_facts: Wednesday looks dry, which makes it a good day for outdoor plans.
There's a chance of snow in the higher mountains late in the week.
stories.why: Enjoy the mild days, and maybe cover sensitive plants and dig out a warm layer for the weekend.

stories.headline: Chris Brown and Usher Bring Back the Duets in Atlanta
stories.summary: After fans complained that Thursday's Atlanta show skipped their joint songs, Chris Brown and Usher performed "Back to Sleep" and the "It Depends" remix together on Friday. Their "R&B Tour" has been a huge seller, and Atlanta's five-show run set a record for Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
key_facts: The tour grossed $284.7 million from the first 36 shows through October 3.
They were the first co-headliners to top the monthly touring chart.
The remaining Atlanta dates are November 8, 10 and 11.
disputed: Confirmed: The duets returned Friday, according to TMZ.
Rumor: Speculation about friction between the two singers. Brown told fans not to believe online chatter.
stories.why: Fans spoke up, and the stars listened.

stories.headline: Attorney General Brushes Off Ex-Adviser's Health Policy Claims
stories.summary: Attorney General Todd Blanche on Sunday dismissed corruption allegations from former Trump health adviser Calley Means against senior White House officials. A former FDA commissioner described pressure from tobacco lobbyists, and a Republican congressman called for scrutiny. The dispute is part of a growing rift inside the "MAHA" health movement.
key_facts: Blanche spoke on CNN's "State of the Union" on Sunday.
Means alleges advisers were undermining Trump's health agenda.
disputed: Means' corruption claims are allegations, and the attorney general has dismissed them. The available report doesn't detail the evidence.
stories.why: It raises questions about who is steering federal health policy.
